feature.spot_perp_close_basis.forward: Pairs still open at the accepted end continue after it only where the nightly forward spot preparation has decided a day for them; the research server then admits those days, and a refusal names each symbol's current intervals.

notes: The gte and lte ladders are deliberately different lengths: the negative side truncates at the total-loss floor because every summarized metric is a return ratio and cannot pass -1.
Bucket closure convention: negative values fall right-closed (lo, hi]; non-negative values fall left-closed [lo, hi). This makes every threshold count an exact partial sum of bucket counts.
present + absent equals the occurrence total for every metric. An absent outcome is counted, never implied to be zero.
Rates come from outcomes_summary over all occurrences; page rows are examples, never the denominator.

Horizon completeness: an anchor closer to the record edge than a horizon reads absent for that horizon and is counted absent, never truncated. With the 7d horizon the last seven days of the record are absent at 7d by construction.
Representatives are selected on the named outcome metric over the complete result before paging (representatives_note says so in the bytes): examples of what followed, never rates.

The outcome sort fields order the page only: counts, outcomes_summary, counts_by_symbol, predicate_coverage and representatives are identical under every sort of the same definition. outcome.* remains forbidden in predicates (OUTCOME_IN_PREDICATE).

feature.spot_perp_close_basis exists only for Binance USD-M perpetuals with a qualified same-underlying USDT Binance spot pair (410 accepted and not retired, fewer than the recorded perpetual universe) and only inside that symbol's intervals in feature_scopes. A query must name its symbols and keep its window inside one interval for each; anything else is refused, never answered as absent. Inside an interval, a missing or zero-trade bar on either leg is absent.

Any change to this descriptor is a result-encoding bump, because these lists join the serving cache and ETag keys. usual_bands rides outcome_first_result, so a band change bumps outcome_first_encoding and leaves result_encoding alone.
usual_bands: a reading stands out when any one of its bands holds, never on an absent value. Enum readings are not listed; they stand out on any label other than none or normal.
